STEP 1 - Scene: This is not really a meal; it is a single whole apple (red-yellow, likely a gala or similar variety) resting on a white triangular/rounded dish, photographed from below or at a steep upward angle. The apple sits in the foreground.

STEP 2 - Ruler: The white dish is roughly 30 cm across its longest visible width (it is a wide, shallow dish). The apple is the only food. Using the apple's typical width as a check: the apple appears about 8 cm across in the photo, consistent with a medium apple of ~7.5-8 cm diameter. Vessel area is not needed for the energy estimate since the food is a single whole item.

STEP 3 - Items: One whole apple (raw, with skin, stem visible).

STEP 4 - Area: The apple covers roughly 10-12% of the visible dish area; it is a single countable piece, so area is not the driver here.

STEP 5 - Volume: A medium apple of ~8 cm diameter is roughly spherical, volume ≈ (4/3)π(4 cm)^3 ≈ 268 ml; apples are slightly less than a full sphere, so ~230 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Whole apples have a density close to water, roughly 0.8-0.9 g/ml when counting internal air. Using 230 ml × 0.85 ≈ 195 g. A typical medium apple weighs about 180 g, so I take ~180 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Raw apple ≈ 52 kcal per 100 g. 180 g × 0.52 = about 94 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: One medium apple at roughly 180 g and ~95 kcal is plausible for what is visible.

Total: about 180 g, about 94 kcal.
